                    ### Question
                    Indicate which serum biochemical profile is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Normal calcium; normal phosphate; normal alkaline phosphatases (FA); normal parathyroid hormone (PTH); 25 OH vitamin D low.
opb. Normal calcium; low phosphate; Normal FA; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
opc. Low calcium; high phosphate; FA elevated; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
opd. Normal calcium; normal phosphate; FA elevated; Elevated PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Option opc is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant. The low calcium, high phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatases (FA), and low 25 OH vitamin D levels align with the expected biochemical profile in this condition. The normal PTH level makes secondary hyperparathyroidism less likely, supporting the diagnosis of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency.
